summary.headline: Cosmo First Q2 FY27 consolidated sales rose 51% to Rs 1,388 crore and EBITDA 38% to Rs 177 crore, though normalised EBITDA growth was 24%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached Rs 1,388 crore (up 51% YoY) on 15% volume growth, with raw-material pass-through driving the rest. Reported EBITDA was Rs 177 crore (12.8% margin vs 14.0%), but it included net non-recurring gains of about Rs 18 crore (US customs duty refund of Rs 24.8 crore less Rs 7 crore inventory loss); excluding these, EBITDA was Rs 159 crore, up 24%. Net debt fell to Rs 1,057 crore (1.9x EBITDA) from Rs 1,159 crore in March 2026 despite a Rs 148 crore working-capital build. Management reiterated a focus on specialty mix, ROCE, and reducing net debt by Rs 300-500 crore over two years.

segments.name: Cosmo Films (B2B, BOPP/BOPET)
segments.commentary: Specialty and semi-specialty about 60% of volume; specialty volume up about 20% and H1 specialty revenue up about 20%. Specialty film margin stable near Rs 62/kg. US business volume up 35% YoY, expected about $70 million in FY27.

segments.name: Specialty chemicals (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue up 59% to about Rs 155 crore; Q2 revenue up over 80% on about 60% volume growth; Q2 EBITDA margin 23%. Third-party sales about 17% of Q2 sales. Medium-term target about Rs 500 crore at 20%+ ROCE.

segments.name: Cosmo Plastech (rigid packaging)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue Rs 39 crore (up 90% YoY) at 8% EBITDA margin; second consecutive profitable quarter. H1 revenue Rs 75 crore (up 73%). Brand sales share rose to 67% from 50%.

segments.name: Cosmo Consumer (window film, PPF, ceramic coatings)
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue up 70% and H1 up 2.6x; EBITDA loss Rs 4.5 crore after TV advertising began July 2026. PPF dealers raised from 150 to 250; window film dealers at 150 across more than 100 cities; four car care centres.

segments.name: Zigly (pet care)
segments.commentary: Revenue up 47% in Q2 and 58% in H1 FY27; 48 centres including three hospitals. Services were 68% of offline sales; private label more than doubled YoY.

guidance_outlook: FY27 capex guided at Rs 100-110 crore; FY28 capex estimated at Rs 50-70 crore, mainly maintenance and specialty.
Net debt expected to fall by Rs 300-500 crore over the next two years; no major capex planned in the short term.
FY27 specialty share about 60% of volume; FY28 target 65-70%; medium term close to 80%.
FY27 effective tax rate guided at a -6% to -7% tax credit; Q2 included a one-time Rs 14 crore credit from moving to the new concessional regime.
Consumer and Zigly targeted at more than 60% growth; consumer losses expected for about two years, then tapered as % of revenue. Zigly target of Rs 200 crore revenue by FY30 referenced by analyst.
Renewable power expected to supply about two-thirds of power needs by next year, saving about Rs 25-30 crore a year.
risks_watch: Raw-material price volatility linked to the West Asia conflict; further inventory write-downs or gains could swing quarterly EBITDA.
Port congestion and container delays, which management says are hard to predict.
Commissioning delays on new BOPP lines, and customer approval timelines for the coating and barrier sheet lines.
Consumer and Zigly losses from marketing spend over the next two years, and the unresolved Zigly monetisation route.
Net debt reduction target of Rs 300-500 crore over two years depends on working-capital release and cash flow.
summary.management_tone: Confident on specialty growth, US volumes and the consumer ramp, but cautious and evasive on raw-material direction, port logistics, Zigly monetisation and the currency-note tender, which management declined to discuss under NDA.
key_quotes: Our B2B businesses are profitable, delivering profitable growth and strengthening their market positions through a greater focus on specialty sales.
As mentioned earlier as well, the normalized EBITDA for the Quarter 2 grew 24% year-on-year.
There is a very clear focus to reduce the net debt substantially in next 2 years as no major CAPEX is planned in the short term.

qa_highlights.question: How much more room is there for US topline growth, and how much headroom is there in film capacity utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: US volume grew 35% in the quarter, with FY27 expected at about $70 million and a target above $100 million next year. Film utilisation is about 90%, leaving 8-10% headroom for volume.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 and FY28 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is Rs 100-110 crore. FY28 capex is estimated at Rs 50-70 crore, mainly maintenance plus some specialty spend, though not yet finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the BOPP spread look flat versus Q1 once the one-offs are stripped out?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 BOPP was Rs 30/kg and Q2 was Rs 29/kg on a like-for-like basis. The Q2 figure includes a Rs 7 crore inventory loss, while Q1 included an inventory gain, so the reconciliation is not direct.

qa_highlights.question: Is Zigly monetisation progressing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is still evaluating options to bring out Zigly's value without adding to Cosmo's balance sheet. It will update the exchanges when there is something concrete.

qa_highlights.question: How will the consumer losses evolve and when could the business break even?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects losses for about two years while marketing continues. Excluding advertising and marketing, the business is close to operational break-even. Management declined to give a break-even revenue number.

qa_highlights.question: What is the JV with a Korean entity and what revenue will the two new lines add?
qa_highlights.answer: The Korea JV is for specialty volumes; approvals are phased and margins are expected over three to five years. Management said both new lines need customer approvals, so revenue will ramp quarter on quarter. Coating adds about US$0.70-1.00/kg over base film and the barrier sheet about US$0.70/kg.

capex_capacity: FY27 capex guided at Rs 100-110 crore; FY28 capex estimated at Rs 50-70 crore, mainly maintenance plus some specialty-linked spend, plan not yet finalised
Capex cycle of roughly Rs 1,250-1,300 crore over the last three years; majority of debt tied to growth capex already in the September 2026 balance sheet; no major capex planned in the short term
16,000 tonne high-end chemical coated film line to be commissioned in H2 FY27; management expects to fill this capacity over two to three years; capex already largely included in Q2 financials
9-layer barrier sheet line with 10,000 metric tonne annual capacity in H2 FY27, with a very modest capex; Cosmo already runs one barrier sheet line and is adding a second

Most BOPP lines to be commissioned over the next two years; management noted some lines may be deferred. Current film utilisation about 90%, with 8-10% headroom. A new coating line was recently commissioned
Renewable power expected to be about two-thirds of power needs by next year, with estimated annual savings of Rs 25-30 crore
demand_pricing: Consolidated Q2 volume up 15% YoY; revenue up 51% with raw-material price pass-through. Specialty volume up about 20% in Q2; specialty and semi-specialty about 60% of total volume
US business volume up 35% YoY in Q2; FY27 expected at about $70 million (FY22 peak $60 million, FY26 about $50 million); FY28 target above $100 million

BOPP gross margin Rs 29/kg in Q2 vs Rs 30/kg in Q1 FY27 and Rs 22/kg a year ago; BOPET Rs 12/kg vs Rs 9/kg in Q1; specialty film margin about Rs 62/kg; semi-specialty margin fell to about Rs 40/kg from about Rs 45/kg on customer and product mix
Specialty chemicals: third-party sales about 17% of Q2 sales; management expects the third-party share to rise towards 50:50 over the medium to long term

Cosmo Consumer: PPF market about Rs 500 crore growing about 30% a year, penetration 1-2% vs about 15% in China; PPF dealers raised from 150 to 250; window film dealers about 150 across more than 100 cities

Raw-material prices rose further in the current month on West Asia crisis; port congestion improved QoQ in Q2 but recurred in the current quarter; Q3 seasonally mixed due to Christmas exports and Diwali

growth.why: Management guides US business to about $70 million in FY27 (vs ~$50 million FY26), consumer and Zigly growth above 60%, and specialty mix ~60% in FY27 rising to 65-70% in FY28; delivery rests on a 16,000 t coated film line and 10,000 MT barrier sheet line due H2 FY27 plus ~90% film utilisation with 8-10% headroom, but BOPP line additions are only partly specified and some may be deferred.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 16,000 tonne coated film line and 10,000 MT barrier sheet line both due H2 FY27 and already under construction, while most BOPP lines come over two years but some may be deferred.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Consolidated volume up 15% in Q2, US volume up 35% with FY27 guided at about $70 million vs about $50 million in FY26, and film utilisation about 90% with 8-10% headroom.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is Rs 100-110 crore and FY28 is estimated at Rs 50-70 crore, mainly maintenance and specialty; management said no major capex is planned in the short term, though the 90% utilisation keeps some pressure on.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is confident on specialty growth (about 20% volume), US volumes and consumer growth above 60%, but the Q2 reported figure included one-offs and raw-material direction is uncertain.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw-material prices rose further on the West Asia crisis, port congestion recurred in the current quarter, and commissioning or customer-approval delays could push out the new lines.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Coated high-end film line (16,000 t) and 9-layer barrier sheet line (10,000 MT) due H2 FY27, with customer approvals phased so revenue ramps quarter on quarter.

rows.label: Net debt cut by Rs 300-500 crore over two years
rows.why: Net debt fell to Rs 1,057 crore (1.9x EBITDA) from Rs 1,159 crore, but a Rs 148 crore working-capital build and lower one-off gains make the target dependent on cash release.

rows.label: US business to about $70 million in FY27, above $100 million in FY28
rows.why: US volume grew 35% in Q2 and FY27 is guided at about $70 million vs about $50 million in FY26, with FY28 target above $100 million.

rows.label: Zigly monetisation route
rows.why: Management is still evaluating options to unlock Zigly value without adding to the balance sheet and will update exchanges only when concrete; Zigly revenue grew 47% in Q2.
